title: When the Summer Falls
premise: Odile Joubert has built a careful life out of other people's words, ghostwriting a rival author's memoirs while guarding a decade of anonymous letters that once kept her heart alive. When the letter writer — Elias Vane, her late brother's best friend and the man she blamed for the accident — moves into the neighboring cottage, Odile must confront the truth she buried: she ended their correspondence out of guilt, not anger. As the memoir deadline collides with a town fight over her grandmother's inherited orchard, Odile and Elias are forced to choose between duty and each other. She forgives herself at last, publishes under her own name, and chooses love in the present tense.
about_author: Paloma Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's love letters before writing her own stories. She lives on a windswept coast where she tends an untidy garden and believes every silence hides a letter worth answering.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She delivers chapters of a rival's memoir to her agent while hiding her own abandoned manuscript in a drawer. Establishes her self-erasure and the letters she rereads but never answers. Emotional beat: quiet ache of a life lived secondhand.

chapters.title: Moving Day
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A removal van arrives at the long-empty cottage next door; she recognizes Elias Vane before he sees her and retreats behind her hedge. Ten years of blame resurface. Emotional beat: panic disguised as composure.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Owes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The town council threatens to rezone her inherited orchard for development; her grandmother's will requires she live there two full seasons to keep it. Duty tightens. Emotional beat: resentment toward an inheritance that imprisons as much as it shelters.

chapters.title: First Words After Ten Years
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He knocks with a borrowed ladder and an apology ten years overdue. Their exchange is civil, brittle, loaded. He reveals he never stopped writing to her — the letters stopped coming back marked 'return to sender.' Emotional beat: the ground shifting beneath old certainties.

chapters.title: The Rival's Deadline
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her client Camille demands a scandalous chapter about a lost summer romance — one that suspiciously mirrors Odile's own. She realizes Camille knows more than she should. Emotional beat: fear that her past is being stolen and weaponized.

chapters.title: Ladders and Lemons
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Forced cooperation harvesting the orchard before a storm; banter thaws into real conversation. Elias admits he was driving the night her brother died — a truth she already knew, but hearing it lands differently now. Emotional beat: grief shared instead of hoarded.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback chapter: the decade of letters, his side of the silence, why he finally came. He wrote the last one unmailed, carried in his coat pocket. Emotional beat: devotion that survived being unanswered.

chapters.title: Camille's Gambit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Camille publishes an excerpt online — Odile's private story, barely disguised, credited to Camille. Public humiliation; the town reads it over breakfast. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal, and the temptation to disappear again.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Elias gives her the final unsent letter; reading it, she understands he took the blame for a decision her brother made too. Her hatred loses its foundation. Emotional beat: mourning the years spent punishing the wrong person — including herself.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A festival night, wine, near-kiss interrupted by Camille's arrival and a public accusation that Odile ghosted the memoir. Elias defends her without knowing it's true. Emotional beat: longing curdled by shame.

chapters.title: Confession in Draft Form
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She confesses the ghostwriting to Elias, expecting disgust; instead he asks why she keeps hiding the truest thing she writes. First real fight, first real honesty. Emotional beat: terror and relief of being fully seen.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Council hearing on the orchard; Camille backs the developers, offering Odile a byline if she testifies the land is worthless. Odile refuses publicly, claiming her grandmother's name — and her own. Emotional beat: first act of self-forgiveness made visible.

chapters.title: What Camille Holds
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Her motive revealed: she loved Elias once, recognized Odile's letters in his stories years ago, and has been writing her rival's memoir around a life she envied. Emotional beat: envy dressed as ambition, loneliness beneath control.

chapters.title: The Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A storm damages half the orchard; the town that read Camille's excerpt shows up anyway to help save the trees. Elias and Odile work side by side until dawn. Emotional beat: belonging arriving unasked-for.

chapters.title: Deadline and Decision
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Camille threatens legal exposure unless Odile finishes the memoir silently. Odile drafts her resignation letter — then hesitates, because finishing it means controlling how the story ends. Emotional beat: agency replacing victimhood.

chapters.title: The Chapter That Was Mine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She writes the lost-summer chapter truthfully, in her own voice, and sends it to Camille as her final contribution — daring her to publish it honestly or not at all. Emotional beat: reclaiming authorship of her own history.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A job offer abroad forces Elias's decision; he won't ask Odile to choose him after a decade of asking nothing. He begins packing. Misunderstanding hardens into distance. Emotional beat: love retreating into old habits of self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She finds the cottage empty except for the box of every returned letter, each annotated in his hand with what he wished he'd said. She runs through rain to the station. Emotional beat: desperation transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: Platform Nine
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The confrontation at the station: both say the unforgivable truths aloud — his silence, her blame, her ghosting, his leaving. Neither boards the train. Emotional beat: rupture becoming repair.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Camille publishes the memoir with Odile's chapter intact and credited after the excerpt scandal turns public opinion. Odile signs a contract for her own novel under her real name. Emotional beat: vindication that feels less sweet than freedom.

chapters.title: The Second Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. One year later: the orchard survives its rezoning vote, the cottage is no longer empty, and Odile writes in present tense. Elias plants a tree for her brother. Emotional beat: grief integrated, love chosen daily.

chapters.title: When the Summer Falls
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing letter format. She writes a letter at last — not to the past, but forward, to whoever needs permission to forgive themselves. Final image: two names on a manuscript, side by side. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
